skill.name: npm-release
skill.description: Guide release managers through versioning, changelog updates, git tagging, GitHub release creation, npm publishing, and rollback steps for cc-devflow.
skill.summary: Runs a structured cc-devflow npm release checklist from preflight checks to publish verification.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are markdown fence or inline-command false positives, not hidden code execution. The skill still contains real high-impact release instructions, including git pushes, GitHub release creation, npm publish, npm unpublish, and remote tag deletion. It should require explicit confirmation before any network write, publish, rollback, or remote rewrite command.

remediation.issue: Publishing and rollback commands can mutate npm and GitHub state.
remediation.suggestion: Add mandatory confirmation gates before npm publish, npm unpublish, git push, tag deletion, and GitHub release creation.

remediation.issue: The workflow can rewrite git origin to a hardcoded repository.
remediation.suggestion: Require repository identity checks before changing remotes, and warn users not to run the command outside cc-devflow.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not verify npm authentication, ownership, or two-factor requirements.
remediation.suggestion: Add checks for npm login, package ownership, token scope, and two-factor authentication before publishing.

static_findings.snippet: Add new version section at the top (after `---`):
| Check status | `git status` | Verify clean state |
| Check version | `grep version package.json` | Current version |
| Create commit | `git commit -m "chore(release): ..."` | Commit version bump |
| Create tag | `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "..."` | Tag release |
| Push commits | `git push origin main` | Push to GitHub |
| Push tags | `git push origin vX.Y.Z` | Push tag to GitHub |
| Publish npm | `npm publish` | Publish to registry |
**Fix**: Run `npm publish --dry-run` first to catch issues

content.value_statement: Manual npm releases can drift across package versions, changelogs, tags, and registry state. This skill provides a step-by-step cc-devflow release workflow with verification and rollback guidance.
actual_capabilities: Checks branch, working tree, current package version, and recent git history.
Guides changelog and package version updates for patch, minor, or major releases.
Creates release commit and annotated git tag instructions.
Documents pushing commits, creating GitHub releases, and publishing to npm.
Provides troubleshooting for GitHub connectivity and SSH remote setup.
Provides rollback steps for npm unpublish, tag deletion, and commit revert.
limitations: Designed specifically for cc-devflow, not arbitrary npm packages.
Does not verify npm ownership, tokens, or two-factor authentication state.
Does not automate CI tests or inspect package contents beyond dry-run guidance.
Pre-release and beta release flows need adaptation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Versioned Release
use_cases.description: Sync the package version, changelog, release commit, and git tag before publishing.

use_cases.title: Publish With Verification
use_cases.description: Follow dry-run, npm publish, and post-release checks in a consistent order.

use_cases.title: Recover a Bad Release
use_cases.description: Use rollback guidance for npm unpublish, tag cleanup, revert, and patch re-release decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start Release Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the npm-release skill to guide me through a patch release for cc-devflow. Begin with pre-release checks and stop before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Release Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the npm-release workflow to draft a changelog entry for version X.Y.Z from these changes: [paste changes].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Full Publish
prompt_templates.prompt: Use npm-release to plan a minor release from version A.B.C to X.Y.Z. Include versioning, commit, tag, GitHub release, dry-run, publish, and verification checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Failed Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use npm-release to handle a bad npm release for version X.Y.Z. Compare unpublish, tag deletion, revert, and patch release options before any command runs.

output_examples.input: I need to publish cc-devflow version 2.5.0 after a minor feature release.
output: Confirms clean main branch, pushed commits, and current package version.
Guides changelog entry, version bump, release commit, annotated tag, dry-run, publish, and verification.

output_examples.input: The release pushed to git, but npm publish failed.
output: Separates local, GitHub, and npm registry state before retrying.
Recommends dry-run checks and confirms whether the existing tag still points to the intended commit.

output_examples.input: Version 2.4.4 was published with a critical bug.
output: Checks whether npm unpublish is still allowed for the affected version.
Plans tag cleanup, commit revert, bug fix, and new patch release steps.

best_practices: Run the dry-run publish step before any real npm publish action.
Confirm package version, changelog version, git tag, and registry version all match.
Require explicit human approval before pushing tags, publishing, unpublishing, or changing remotes.
anti_patterns: Do not use this workflow on a dirty branch or the wrong repository.
Do not publish when changelog, package version, and git tag disagree.
Do not run rollback commands before confirming npm and GitHub state.

faq.question: What package is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for releasing the cc-devflow npm package.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance. Users should approve all publishing, pushing, remote changes, and rollback commands.

faq.question: Does it support beta or pre-release versions?
faq.answer: No. The skill says beta and pre-release flows need adaptation.

faq.question: Can it create a GitHub release?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes optional GitHub CLI release creation guidance.

faq.question: Does it verify npm authentication?
faq.answer: No. It does not check npm login state, ownership, token scope, or two-factor authentication.

faq.question: What rollback support is included?
faq.answer: It documents npm unpublish timing, tag deletion, commit revert, bug fixes, and patch re-release.
